- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.68 or 82.31), then corrects with a downward bias.
- Underestimates in the middle-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when true values show mean reversion toward prior levels.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the 3rd–5th day, then gradually adjust downward — suggesting a lag in recognizing recent volatility.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent peaks — implies failure to account for price exhaustion or policy-induced cooling.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model still forecasts upward — indicates failure to recognize mean reversion or policy-induced floor.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the 1st–3rd day, then become more accurate later — suggests model overreacts to recent volatility and underweights long-term trends.
